Keeping peptides cool in Corona

Chino Airport, at 650 feet, is the nearest NOAA normals station, about 8.8 miles north-northwest of Corona's center point.5810 August there averages a high of 96.3 °F and a low of 63.2 °F; December averages 68.7 °F and 40.4 °F.5 The station logs about 99 days a year at 90 °F or more and 23.3 days at 100 °F or more, plus 11.4 nights at or below freezing.4 Riverside Municipal Airport, about 9.6 miles northeast, sees a similar 21.7 days at 100 °F or more but only 3.5 freezing nights.11810 Corona's weather can test a parcel at both ends of the scale.

For freeze-dried powder, cold is the smaller risk. Peptide makers store it frozen for the long term: Bachem advises below -15 °C and GenScript -20 °C.67 Repeated freezing and thawing is the hazard. GenScript warns that peptides put through freeze-thaw cycles are prone to degradation, and that splitting a peptide into single-use aliquots cuts both the number of cycles and the air exposure. It also advises against opening the stock vial again and again.7 The reconstitution guide covers the lab steps, and the storage guide covers the rest.

About Corona

Corona had 161,734 residents on July 1, 2025, third among the county's 28 incorporated cities and up about 2.9% since 2020.1 It covers 39.904 square miles of land.8 Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas 92879, 92880, 92881 and 92882 hold most of the city. Area 92883 reaches into it but lies mostly outside, and a slice of the city sits in 92503, which it shares with Riverside.9 The city was established in 1886, incorporated in 1896 and runs its own electric utility.3

Once called South Riverside, Corona is still known as the Circle City. Grand Boulevard, laid out in 1886, forms a circle about a mile across around the original townsite, and international road races ran on it in 1913, 1914 and 1916.2 The Mediterranean Revival Historic Civic Center opened in 1923 as the city's second high school and served as City Hall from 1962 to 2005.12

Corona Regional Medical Center is the city's second largest employer, with 1,250 employees in 2025.3 The state's health facility office lists two licensed campuses: a general acute care hospital with a basic emergency department and 160 licensed beds, and a consolidated campus with 99.1314 In neighboring Norco, Naval Surface Warfare Center Corona Division has about 1,800 civilian staff and more than 2,000 contractors. It calls itself the Navy's only independent assessment agent, working on data analytics, fleet training systems, ordnance engineering and measurement accuracy.15

Corona-Norco Unified School District is the largest employer, with 5,172 people in 2025. Monster Energy (1,080) and Fender USA Corona (903) are also in the top five.3

Frequently asked questions

Corona sits where four counties meet. Does that change how an order is delivered?

No. Corona is a Riverside County city at the junction of Riverside, Orange, Los Angeles and San Bernardino counties, served by Interstates 91 and 15.3 None of that affects an order: a Corona address is handled by shipping from the USA and Canada, like every order across the United States. The shipping page says what is and is not yet confirmed about timing and charges, and the contact page takes questions.

Does Corona get cold enough to freeze a parcel?

On some winter nights, yes. Chino Airport, the nearest NOAA normals station, averages 11.4 nights a year at or below 32 °F, with a December average low of 40.4 °F.45 For freeze-dried powder, cold is the smaller risk: peptide makers store it frozen for the long term.67 Repeated freezing and thawing is the real hazard, and GenScript warns that peptides put through freeze-thaw cycles are prone to degradation.7 Bring parcels in rather than leaving them out overnight.

Is Temescal Valley part of Corona?

No. Temescal Valley is an unincorporated census-designated place about 9 miles southeast of Corona's center point.8 The two share ZIP Code Tabulation Area 92883: about a third of its land lies in the Temescal Valley census area and only a small part in Corona.9 Each place has its own page here: see Peptides in Temescal Valley for that community.
